transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I can’t stop thinking about how the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up. I feel like people at the warehouse, or when I go salsa dancing, are noticing it all the time, even though they tell me they don’t see anything.
Deep down, do you ever consider that your face might actually look normal and this might be in your head, or are you completely certain that the deformity is real?

I mean, people keep telling me they don’t see it, so I guess part of me wonders. But it really looks crooked to me. I can’t stop focusing on the left side of my face, and it feels like people at work or salsa night have to notice it.
Do you find yourself frequently checking your face in mirrors or other reflective surfaces throughout the day?

Yeah. Before I go back out on the inventory floor, I keep checking in the bathroom mirror. I’ll fix my cap and rub at the same spot on my face over and over. Sometimes I get so caught up doing that I’m late getting back, and my picking numbers fall behind. My boss has gotten on me about it.

latest_inference.note: The repetitive mirror checking, touching/rubbing of the face, and camouflaging behaviors, coupled with significant occupational impairment and partial insight, fulfill the diagnostic criteria for body dysmorphic disorder (classified under F45.2 in ICD-10), ruling out primary social phobia (F40.1) and general OCD (F42).
